Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Practice Plan — Thursday AM, three lanes for one squad of twelve, three lanes, one coach
Resource limits: three lanes, one set of starting blocks, one coach on deck, two and a half hours of pool time.
Everything must be finished by 150 minutes of pool time.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Practice Plan — Thursday AM, three lanes

We have three lanes for two and a half hours and one set of starting blocks. Lane 1 is the sprint group, lane 2 the middle distance, lane 3 the distance group. Everything except the sprint set runs in all three lanes at once; the sprint set runs one lane at a time off the blocks, so lanes wait their turn.

On deck
Brief the squad on the pool deck: what the morning is, who is in which lane, 5 minutes.
Watch the warm-up from the deck and fix anything ugly; 15 minutes.

Warm-up
All three lanes start together: 20 minutes, 800 easy, mixed stroke, breathing every five on the last hundred.

Whiteboard
Call the lanes to the wall when the warm-up is done and walk the main set on the whiteboard; 5 minutes. Nobody pushes off until the board is done.

Kick set
20 minutes of kick, boards for lanes 1 and 2, vertical kick for lane 3, once the whiteboard talk is over.

Main set
Lane 1: 30 to 50 minutes, 40 minutes is the plan.
Lane 2: 30 to 50 minutes, 45 minutes is the plan.
Lane 3: 30 to 50 minutes, 50 minutes is the plan.
Every lane swims its own main set and the sprint set does not start until the last lane is in.

Sprint set
One set of blocks, one lane at a time, 10 minutes each.
Lane 1 goes first, off the blocks, dive starts, 25s flat out.
Lane 2 goes second, same thing, on the lane 1 group's last dive.
Lane 3 goes third and gets the extra rest it will need.
Time the sprints from the deck: 30 minutes, stopwatch and the wall clock.

Cooldown
All three lanes cool down together once the last sprint is in: 10 minutes, 300 easy backstroke and breaststroke.

Debrief
10 minutes on the deck at the end: splits, what to fix, Saturday's meet.

Note
The main set is the only place a lane can run long and the only place the plan gives them room to. Everything after it is a join: the blocks cannot be shared and the cooldown starts together or it does not start at all.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

**Read-back**

This is an on-deck session plan for one swim squad of twelve split into three lane groups — lane 1 sprint, lane 2 middle distance, lane 3 distance — run by a single coach on the deck, and it plays out across three parallel lanes that occasionally have to become one queue. There are three pooled resources that exist only once or only in limited supply, and each one is the reason the plan has a join in it: three lanes (so lane-specific work — the main sets — can run in parallel, but only one lane group can ever be on the one set of starting blocks), one set of starting blocks (so the sprint set is strictly one lane at a time, 10 minutes each, lane 1 then lane 2 then lane 3, with lane 2 pushing off around lane 1's last dive and lane 3 getting deliberately extra rest), and one coach on deck (so every coaching task — the 5-minute brief, the 15 minutes watching warm-up, the 5-minute whiteboard, the 30 minutes timing sprints with a stopwatch, the 10-minute debrief — is serial and belongs to one person, not to a lane). The whole thing must be done inside 150 minutes of pool time, and the source's own arithmetic lands right on that ceiling: a 20-minute warm-up, a 5-minute whiteboard talk nobody may push off before, a 20-minute kick set, main sets of 30–50 minutes planned at 40/45/50, a 30-minute block-limited sprint set, a 10-minute cooldown and a 10-minute debrief. Two moments have to be held and one has to be ready: nothing pushes off into the kick set until the whiteboard is finished, the sprint set does not start until the *last* lane is in off its main set, and the cooldown starts together for all three lanes once the last sprint is in — so the main set is the only stretch where a lane has any slack, and every lane's drift has to be absorbed long lanes run against the single block queue and the single coach clock.

One caution on the source: nothing looks truncated — all nine sections (on deck, warm-up, whiteboard, kick set, main set, sprint set, cooldown, debrief, note) are present, and the note explicitly names the main set as the only place a lane can run long. What is *not* in the text is a wall-clock start time or date, so the 150-minute ceiling is a relative deadline measured from the start of pool time, not a timestamp, and "lane 3 gets the extra rest it will need" is a stated intent without a number to it.

```json
{
  "summary": "A 150-minute Thursday AM swim practice for one squad of twelve split into three lane groups (lane 1 sprint, lane 2 middle distance, lane 3 distance), run by one coach on deck. Three lanes freed the main sets to run in parallel, but one set of starting blocks and one coach force joins: the sprint set runs one lane at a time (10 minutes each, lane 1 then 2 then 3, lane 2 starting on lane 1's last dive, lane 3 given extra rest), and every coaching task is a single serial resource. Nothing pushes off until the whiteboard talk ends, the sprint set waits for the last lane out of its main set, and cooldown starts together once the last sprint is in. Everything must finish within 150 minutes of pool time, which the plan's own time adds up to almost exactly, leaving the variable main set (30-50 min, planned 40/45/50) as the only slack in the morning. The source names no clock time or date, so the deadline is relative to the start of pool time.",
  "servesOrScale": "12 swimmers in 3 lanes (sprint / middle distance / distance), 1 coach on deck",
  "deadline": "T+150 minutes of pool time (Thursday AM; no wall-clock start time or date given in the source, so no absolute timestamp)",
  "constraints": [
    "three lanes — one per group, main sets run in all lanes at once",
    "one set of starting blocks — sprint set strictly one lane at a time, 10 minutes each, lane 1 → lane 2 → lane 3",
    "one coach on deck — brief, deck warm-up watch, whiteboard, sprint timing and debrief are all serial on one person",
    "150 minutes of total pool time, with everything finished by then",
    "kick set is gated on the whiteboard talk finishing (nobody pushes off before)",
    "sprint set is a join on the last lane out of its main set",
    "cooldown is a join on the last sprint being in — it starts all three lanes together",
    "main set is variable (30-50 min; 40/45/50 planned) and is the only place a lane may run long",
    "lane 2's sprint starts on lane 1 group's last dive; lane 3 gets extra rest before its sprint"
  ]
}
```

**The model, in my own words**

A **track** is one strictly sequential line of work — its steps run one after another and can never overlap, so any two things that happen at the same time have to live in different tracks (which is exactly why the three lanes and the coach's own deck work need separate tracks here). Every **step** carries exactly one duration kind and nothing else: `fixed` with `seconds`, `variable` with `minSeconds`/`maxSeconds`/`defaultSeconds`, or `indefinite`, which runs until the person on deck ends it. A **startTrigger** is how a step finds its place in time — `programStart` or `programStartOffset` off the clock, `afterStep` / `afterStepWithBuffer` off another step, `manual` when a human taps, `onAbort`, or a `compound` waiting on all/any of several — and `stepId`s are unique across the entire program, not just within a track, because every trigger reference is a global lookup. Each step also declares the **task** it occupies, and every distinct task in the program needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry whose `maxConcurrent` is the thing that stops two steps sharing one oven, one thermocycler, one set of blocks or one PA system. Repeated work of the same shape (n trays, n tubes, n aircraft) is expressed once as `replicates: {count, mode}` on a single step — never as hand-copied steps or tracks — with followers chained via `instances: "each"` per repetition, the join written as `instances: "all"`, and `replicates.maxInFlight: k` when the holding area between repetitions only fits k so the *upstream* step gets held back rather than a finished item getting stranded. In this plan the repeated shape is the one thing a lane cannot share — the single set of blocks, run once per lane group — so it belongs in one step with `replicates` and a barrier after it, not three copies.

**Resource constraints I expect this workout to need**

- `lane` — `maxConcurrent: 3`; twelve swimmers in three lane groups (4 per lane), and three lanes genuinely exist, which is what lets the three main sets and the warm-up/kick/cooldown run in parallel.
- `blocks` — `maxConcurrent: 1`; one set of starting blocks, so the sprint set is a queue: one lane group at a time, 10 minutes each, lane 1 → lane 2 → lane 3.
- `coach` — `maxConcurrent: 1`; one coach on deck, and every coaching act (5-minute brief, 15-minute warm-up watch, 5-minute whiteboard, 30-minute stopwatch timing of the sprints, 10-minute debrief) is serial on that one person.

I am deliberately **not** adding a separate task for the whiteboard, the stopwatch or the pool deck wall: those are not scarce in the source, whereas lanes, blocks and the coach are the three lines the plan actually says can't be shared. The squad's *people* are modeled inside those tracks (three lane groups of four), not as a fourth constraint, because twelve swimmers never contend for anything the source names — they contend for lanes and for blocks, which are already capped.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work and never overlap, so simultaneous work goes in separate tracks; each step has exactly one duration kind (fixed / variable / indefinite); a startTrigger links a step to the clock (programStart, programStartOffset, manual) or to another step (afterStep, afterStepWithBuffer, onAbort, compound); stepIds are unique across the whole program because triggers reference them globally; every task a step occupies needs a resourceConstraints entry and its maxConcurrent is what serializes shared gear; repeated work is one step with replicates (count + serial/parallel/stagger), followers chained with instances \"each\", the join written instances \"all\", and maxInFlight when a holding area only fits k.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "lane", "maxConcurrent": 3, "note": "three lanes exist; 12 swimmers in 3 lane groups (4 per lane) — main sets, warm-up, kick and cooldown run in all three at once" },
    { "task": "blocks", "maxConcurrent": 1, "note": "one set of starting blocks — sprint set is one lane group at a time, 10 minutes each, lane 1 then lane 2 then lane 3" },
    { "task": "coach", "maxConcurrent": 1, "note": "one coach on deck — brief, warm-up watch, whiteboard, sprint timing with the stopwatch and the debrief are all serial on this one person" }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```

Turn 3 of 4 — extraction. Steps only: no tracks, no triggers, no program JSON.

- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or start_workout), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="150 minutes of pool time" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
